semantic_adjudication.basis: NL1 requirement, PlantUML source lines 4/11/18 declaring 'Idle' in three blocks, PlantUML global name resolution semantics, closed model single-state confirmation, working_contract scope mapping.
semantic_adjudication.reason: The exact source facts show three declarations of 'Idle' at PlantUML lines 4, 11, and 18 within three different blocks (Frontend, Pedestrian, RearEnd). PlantUML state names are global identifiers—a well-defined language semantic that causes same-named states to resolve to a single entity regardless of enclosing block. The closed model confirms a single Frontend.Idle state, and every initial entry from the other two blocks targets this shared state. NL1 requires three independent regions, which presupposes each region has its own distinct states. The global-name collision means Pedestrian and RearEnd cannot have their own Idle state, undermining their independence as separate regions. No competent defeater applies—the PlantUML language semantics are deterministic and well-defined.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: Each block that declares a state named Idle must obtain its own distinct state; PlantUML global name resolution causes the three declarations (lines 4, 11, 18) in Frontend, Pedestrian, and RearEnd to collapse into a single shared state, violating the NL1 requirement for three independent regions.

issues.basis: NL3 text 'orthogonal regions... concurrent activation'; PlantUML CollisionAvoidanceSystem body shows three child composites without -- separators; canonical_source_ir concurrent_regions count=0; FCSTM model text shows Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian, UnspecifiedInitial as sequential children of CollisionAvoidanceSystem; inspection_equivalent_facts state inventory confirms single-region structure.
issues.expected: CollisionAvoidanceSystem must contain orthogonal regions (separated by UML region delimiters) that enable concurrent activation of the three collision avoidance controls (Frontend, Rear-End, Pedestrian).
issues.observed: CollisionAvoidanceSystem contains Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian, and UnspecifiedInitial as direct children in a single implicit region. No region separators (-- or --left--/--right--) exist in the PlantUML source or the FCSTM model. The canonical IR reports concurrent_regions count=0. All three sub-composites are in the same sequential region, not in independent orthogonal regions.
issues.reason: The region_structure contract requires orthogonal regions within the active mode. The cross-view contrast shows: (1) the PlantUML source has no region separators within CollisionAvoidanceSystem, (2) the canonical IR reports zero concurrent regions, and (3) the FCSTM model places all children in a single implicit region. The NL explicitly requires 'orthogonal regions' enabling 'concurrent activation', which is a UML region-structure property not present in the model. No frozen predicate directly checks region structure, so this remains a predicate-null candidate.
issues.requirement_quote: The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The three sub-composites (Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian) do exist as children of CollisionAvoidanceSystem, and one could argue they provide structural separation even without explicit region delimiters. However, without region separators, UML semantics place them in a single implicit region where only one can be active at a time, which contradicts the NL requirement for 'concurrent activation' of different controls.
issues.title: CollisionAvoidanceSystem lacks orthogonal region separators for concurrent collision avoidance controls

The source has none within CollisionAvoidanceSystem. The compiler's synthetic UnspecifiedInitial is not an author-specified entry and does not target any required child region. The verify facts confirm all three sub-composites are unreachable. This is a structural gap between the NL requirement for active regions and the model's lack of any entry mechanism to them.

However, in UML state machine semantics, a composite state requires an explicit initial entry to specify which child state(s) are entered upon activation. Without it, the children have no defined entry behavior, which is exactly what the UnspecifiedInitial synthetic state represents.

issues.basis: exact_source_inventory tr_0009: source=@initial:CollisionAvoidanceSystem.Pedestrian, target=CollisionAvoidanceSystem.Frontend.Idle; PlantUML line 18 [*] --> Idle within Pedestrian body (no local Idle defined); FCSTM state:InvalidInitialtr_0009:line:31 with explicit 'outside child scope' name; FCSTM transition:line:32 [*] -> InvalidInitialtr_0009 within scope Pedestrian; working_contract confirms compiler:state:...InvalidInitialtr_0009 as synthetic_state.
issues.expected: Pedestrian's initial entry (from its local [*]) must target a valid child state within Pedestrian's own scope, enabling the pedestrian collision avoidance sub-machine to initialize independently.
issues.observed: The source transition tr_0009 declares [*] within Pedestrian targeting CollisionAvoidanceSystem.Frontend.Idle, which is outside Pedestrian's scope. The compiler created a synthetic state InvalidInitialtr_0009 (line:31, named 'PlantUML initial target outside child scope: CollisionAvoidanceSystem.Frontend.Idle') and the FCSTM initial entry transition:line:32 targets this synthetic placeholder. No valid local operating state exists within Pedestrian to serve as the initial entry target.
issues.reason: The source declares an initial entry within Pedestrian (tr_0009) but its target resolves to Frontend.Idle, which is outside Pedestrian's containment scope. The compiler created a synthetic InvalidInitialtr_0009 state. The FCSTM initial entry for Pedestrian (transition:line:32) targets this synthetic state. This mirrors the RearEnd defect and further undermines the NL requirement for three independently operable regions.
issues.requirement_quote: There are three region in this diagram
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The PlantUML author wrote [*] --> Idle within Pedestrian, showing clear intent for a local initial entry. The defect is in scope resolution, not structural intent. However, the closed model as parsed contains no valid local target, making the initial entry malformed in the executable model.
issues.title: Pedestrian initial entry targets out-of-scope Frontend.Idle instead of a valid local state

issues.basis: Derived contract NL-CONTRACT-NL2-DERIVED-INITIAL-ENTRY-1 from NL2; FCSTM transition inventory for scope CollisionAvoidanceSystem: transition:line:39 ([*] -> UnspecifiedInitial) is the only initial entry; no transition with source=[*] and target=Frontend exists in scope CollisionAvoidanceSystem; working contract classifies UnspecifiedInitial as compiler_owned synthetic_state; verify_facts initial-entry:transition:line:39 proved (the synthetic edge exists) but no initial entry to operating children exists.
issues.expected: CollisionAvoidanceSystem must have an initial pseudostate edge to one of its operating child composites (Frontend, RearEnd, or Pedestrian) to establish a well-defined starting configuration from which activation behavior can occur.
issues.observed: The only initial entry edge within CollisionAvoidanceSystem scope is [*] -> UnspecifiedInitial (transition:line:39), where UnspecifiedInitial is a compiler-synthetic placeholder state (working contract: compiler_owned, kind=synthetic_state). No initial edge targets any operating child (Frontend, RearEnd, or Pedestrian). The complete transition inventory for scope CollisionAvoidanceSystem contains no edge from [*] to Frontend, RearEnd, or Pedestrian.
issues.reason: The NL2 activation requirement presupposes the sub-machine starts in a defined state. Cross-view grounding reveals that CollisionAvoidanceSystem lacks any owner-local initial entry to its operating children. The S2 predicate checks for the exact edge [*] -> Frontend in scope CollisionAvoidanceSystem; the complete transition inventory confirms this edge is absent. The existing [*] -> UnspecifiedInitial edge goes to a compiler synthetic, not an operating state.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The compiler created UnspecifiedInitial precisely because the author did not specify an initial state for CollisionAvoidanceSystem, and the intended initial entry might be to a conceptual 'inactive' state that is not explicitly modeled. However, the NL requires the sub-machine to be activatable, which necessitates a concrete starting state from which the activation transition can fire. A synthetic placeholder with no outgoing transitions to operating states does not fulfill this role.
issues.title: CollisionAvoidanceSystem has no owner-local initial entry to an operating child state

issues.basis: Derived contract NL-CONTRACT-NL2-DERIVED-REACHABILITY-1 from NL2; verify_facts check_id 'reachability:state:Frontend:line:7' status=refuted, details reachable_from_initial=false; inspection_equivalent_facts states Frontend reachable_from_initial=false; reachable_state_refs=[state:llms_emp_feedback_final_0047:line:2, state:CollisionAvoidanceSystem:line:6, state:UnspecifiedInitial:line:35] does not include Frontend.
issues.expected: The Frontend composite (the primary operating mode containing the Idle/Braking/Clamping collision avoidance cycle) must be reachable from the root initial state so that the sub-machine can execute its activation and collision avoidance behavior.
issues.observed: Deterministic verify_facts show reachability:state:Frontend:line:7 as refuted with reachable_from_initial=false. Inspection equivalent facts confirm Frontend (state:Frontend:line:7) has reachable_from_initial=false. The reachable state set from initial contains only: root (llms_emp_feedback_final_0047), CollisionAvoidanceSystem, and UnspecifiedInitial. No path exists from the initial state to Frontend because CollisionAvoidanceSystem's initial entry goes to the synthetic UnspecifiedInitial rather than to any operating child, and UnspecifiedInitial has no outgoing transition to Frontend.
issues.reason: The NL2 requires the sub-machine to respond to collision detection by becoming active. The Frontend composite is the only operating mode with non-synthetic leaf states implementing this behavior. Deterministic facts confirm it is unreachable from the root initial state. G1 (path existence from source to target) is refuted for the pair (root, Frontend). This is an independent behavioral consequence from the structural initial_entry defect.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Frontend does have an internal initial entry ([*] -> Idle, transition:line:11), so if Frontend were entered, its internal behavior would work. The unreachability is entirely due to the missing parent-level initial entry, which is captured by the separate derived initial_entry contract. However, reachability from root is an independent property: even with a corrected initial entry, other structural defects (e.g., guarded transitions that are unsatisfiable) could still prevent reachability. The G1 refutation is a fact about the current closed model.
issues.title: Frontend operating mode is unreachable from the root initial state

issues.basis: Derived contract NL-CONTRACT-NL2-DERIVED-EVENT-CONSUMER-1 from NL2; verify_facts check_id 'event-consumer:Collision_Detected' status=refuted, reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]; inspection_equivalent_facts event_consumers[Collision_Detected]: consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:12, transition:line:15, transition:line:18], reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]; diagnostic EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE severity=warning refs=[transition:line:12, transition:line:15, transition:line:18].
issues.expected: The Collision_Detected event must have at least one reachable consumer transition within the CollisionAvoidanceSystem operating scope, so that when a collision is detected the system can actually process the event and activate collision avoidance behavior.
issues.observed: The Collision_Detected event has three declared consumer transitions (transition:line:12, transition:line:15, transition:line:18, all Idle->Braking within Frontend), but none are reachable from the top-level initial entry. Verify_facts show event-consumer:Collision_Detected as refuted with reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]. Inspection equivalent facts confirm the same: consumer_transition_refs are present but reachable_consumer_transition_refs is empty. The diagnostic EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE (severity=warning) explicitly flags this.
issues.reason: The NL2 requires the system to respond to collision detection. The Collision_Detected event is the model's representation of this stimulus. While it has declared consumers, none are reachable, meaning the system can never actually process a collision detection event at runtime. No frozen predicate directly checks reachable event consumer coverage, so predicate_id is null (W1). The precise claim is that the event's operational coverage is zero despite structural declarations existing.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The event IS declared and DOES have structurally valid consumers (the Idle->Braking transitions are well-formed with correct triggers). The failure is purely due to the unreachability of their host state (Frontend/Idle), which is captured by the separate reachability and initial_entry derived contracts. One could argue that fixing the initial entry would automatically fix the consumer coverage, making this a redundant observation. However, event consumer coverage is an independent operational property: it asks whether the event can actually be processed in the running system, not whether it has a structural consumer.
issues.title: Collision_Detected event has no reachable consumer in the operating scope
